Tried using Monday.com for a building project and the interface became totally unusably slow. Unsure if it's been fixed, but it seems like an issue for a billion-dollar company.
Monday is just plain bad. It's slow and not really useful, and looks like a bunch of solutions looking for problems put together in a frenzy.

Moving from Trello to monday.com was the biggest reason the team couldn't deliver an iOS project on time. Management switched for a 'good deal', the team HATED it, and 90% started updating tickets once a week instead of daily because they hated the tool. They went back to Trello.

Uses it at current company and doesn't like it. Jira is far superior, and its integration with other Atlassian products helps. Linking tickets to one another in Monday is really bad, data gets lost all the time, and it's not good for retaining a record of work.
Worked at a company where Monday was the main interface between the back-office and its B2B clients: 'That was about as bad as you can expect.'

One of the worst tools I've ever used, after trying hard for a year. The interface is clunky and slow, and it lets you delete important things by accident. Multiple people in our group fell victim to its non-intuitive UI.
Tried it briefly for a small 5-6 person team. It was slow as hell, so they stopped using it.
Never understood monday.com when similar tools like Asana and Atlassian's products are already popular. It always seemed to relabel known practices with its own terminology.
A client forced us onto Monday, and its un-opinionated style made it quite crappy. You basically have to do whatever all the managers came up with randomly, and it sucked.

Used it a few years ago when it was called dapulse. Really wanted to like it because it was so clean, but it required too much setup and customization, similar to Jira. The team switched back to GitHub issues/projects/milestones.
Used it a few times and found it as good as the others. There's no silver bullet; what works for some companies won't work for others, and the real issues are people issues.
